decision.title: More source code languages, a registration API and run-time languages (packet )

body.p: , after , , , , , , , , . The owner's answer to 's proposal (2026-10-20): TypeScript, TSX and Markdown built in, not Rust or Bash; a public registration API, with tree-sitter's ABI part of the contract; languages supplied at run time from tree-sitter language files, loaded by the host, never by src/. The owner's order: the book (commit 0cad9a1), the tests (a40851e), the implementation (c1a88af), the budgets (10487b2).

item.p: Built-in languages (glossary ): typescript and tsx (tree-sitter-typescript 75b3874; their scanners include ../../common/scanner.h, vendored to third_party/tree-sitter-grammars/common/; TypeScript's queries name JavaScript's package, taken from the vendored javascript grammar as queries/javascript-*.scm), markdown and markdown_inline (tree-sitter-markdown a0a00f8). The vendor script also copies the locals and injections queries and the injection-regex of tree-sitter.json; the seven grammars of were vendored again at their commits (JavaScript gains locals.scm and injections.scm, HTML injections.scm). sxml:code-languages() lists eleven.

Locals (glossary ; tree-sitter's highlight crate): local.scope, local.definition(.*), local.reference captures in document order, a scope stack and a definition list (explicit, ), #set! local.scope-inherits false; a reference finds the innermost earlier definition of its text; definitions and resolved references are local for #is? local/#is-not? local, and a reference takes its definition's highlight ('s "no node is local" is gone).

Injections (glossary , , ): injection.content with injection.language (a capture's text or #set!), injection.self, injection.include-children. The node's range without its named children's (as Neovim and the highlight crate: Markdown's inline nodes hold anonymous tokens of the block grammar) is parsed through tree-sitter's included ranges, so positions are the document's. The language is found by name (registered first), then by the first injection regex that matches (XPath regex, registered first); unknown languages leave the node as it is. The injected tree is written inside the node's element; its document element has language. The option injections (default true) turns it off; the corpus driver parses without injections. One loop over an explicit stack of layers (one per tree), at most 8 injections deep. Not supported: injection.combined (each node is its own document), injection.parent.

Registration API (processor.h, additive after ; glossary ): sxml_source_code_language (name, const struct TSLanguage *grammar, highlights, locals and injections query texts, injection regex), sxml_processor_configuration. source_code_languages (appended, so earlier fields keep their places), sxml_source_code_check_language with sxml_source_code_language_report (problem: name, ABI, which query and its byte offset), and SXML_SOURCE_CODE_MINIMUM_LANGUAGE_ABI 13 to ..._MAXIMUM_... 15, the range tree-sitter 0.27's runtime reads (tree-sitter 0.20 and later). A registered language replaces a built-in one of its name. sxml_processor_initialize refuses empty or odd names (letters, digits, _-+.), NULL grammars, other ABIs and a name twice (cheap: no query is compiled there); a query that does not compile raises sxml:invalid-query when the language is used (an injected language's bad query only drops its highlights). The checks are in src/source_code_check.c, so the processor does not link the grammars. Lifetime: the array, grammars and texts outlive the processor. A TSLanguage is immutable, so a host may share one.

Run-time language files: what works. Native shared libraries (glossary : libtree-sitter-NAME.so, .dylib, .dll, or NAME.so as tree-sitter build writes, exporting tree_sitter_NAME()), loaded by the CLI: --code-language=LIBRARY (repeatable) for sxml xpath, sxml xquery and sxml transform (: one flag; it works on Linux, macOS and Windows; under WASI the platform has no loader and the flag reports "this platform loads no libraries", exit 3, as --allow-file-access has no Windows file system). The name is the file name without directory, extension, lib and tree-sitter-, with - made _; the queries are queries/ beside the library (a grammar repository after tree-sitter build), else ../queries/NAME/ (Neovim's parser/ and queries/ layout); without highlights.scm there, no queries. Errors: a name that names no language (2), a library that does not load or lacks the function (3, with dlerror's text), another ABI or a query that does not fit (1, with the byte offset and the file). The CLI framework gains sxml_cli_library_loader (cli_command.h), the platform layer apps/sxml/platform_library_loader.c (dlopen RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL, dlsym; LoadLibraryW, GetProcAddress), which the platform-layer lint rule names; libraries stay loaded until exit. Test: tree-sitter/run-time-language builds the vendored JSON grammar as a module with the entry point tree_sitter_testjson, no network.

Run-time language files: delayed, with reasons. (a) tree-sitter's WebAssembly language files (tree-sitter-NAME.wasm, web-tree-sitter's) in the JavaScript package: each is a dylink side module that imports the main module's memory, indirect function table, stack pointer, __memory_base/__table_base and libc (malloc, iswspace, ...). sxml.wasm is a WASI SDK static module (not -fPIC/--experimental-pic), exports no table or stack pointer, and its tree-sitter is C inside it, so a language file cannot be linked into it. Doing it means building sxml.wasm as a PIC main module and a small dynamic linker in the package's JavaScript (what web-tree-sitter does): a later packet, medium to large, with its own size cost. (b) The same files natively, through tree-sitter's wasm store (ts_wasm_store_new): it needs wasmtime's C API, a JIT runtime of several MB built with Rust; rejected for sxml, which is a small embeddable C library with no JIT ('s spirit), and native hosts have shared libraries anyway. (c) The host shim (bindings/host) and so Kotlin and Swift: the shim's configuration would pass languages through; Phase 6 is paused (), so it waits for 6.12; a grammar pointer across JNI needs its own design.

Not shipped: Rust and Bash as built-ins (the owner), 's sizes; they are one --code-language away. markdown_inline's wiki_link and tag extensions are not in the generated parser (upstream generates them only with EXTENSION_WIKI_LINK/EXTENSION_TAGS), so their 8 corpus tests fail; one spec test has no divider (an error of the corpus).

Measured (debug ASan/UBSan): tree-sitter/suite 630 of 639 to 1,410 of 1,438 (corpus 1,223 of 1,251, 19 not run; highlights 187 of 187: the 7 locals and 2 injections assertions pass); the baseline is 1,410. The book's chapter: 32 examples, all match ('s 18 updated: a reference to a parameter is variable.parameter). source_code_test gains the checks and registered languages; CLI help goldens show the flag. Sizes: sxml.wasm 9,693,235 / 2,006,198 to 13,425,285 / 2,411,765 (+3,730,635 code and data, 3,671,000 of it the four grammars, 95 % parse tables), budget 14,000,000 / 2,800,000; the CLI module 15,026,404 / 2,696,842, budget 15,500,000 / 2,900,000.
